subject.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports

question: Should direct npm or pnpm global replacement be guarded by this postinstall probe, or should stale-gateway guidance remain exclusively in the managed `openclaw update` lifecycle?
rationale: The canonical reproduction uses direct package-manager rollback that the managed updater cannot own, but this proposal duplicates service and config discovery while adding a new environment surface; maintainers must choose the permanent lifecycle boundary.

options.title: Keep a corrected postinstall guard
options.body: Retain direct package-manager coverage, replace ad hoc config parsing with canonical JSON5/include-aware resolution, and remove or explicitly approve the opt-out variable.

options.title: Keep warnings in update CLI only
options.body: Close or narrow this PR and accept that direct package-manager installs require documented manual restart guidance outside the managed updater.

options.title: Design a service handshake
options.body: Pause both warning approaches and develop a broader package-lifecycle mechanism that identifies and safely stops or restarts the exact managed gateway.

recommendation.title: Keep a corrected postinstall guard
recommendation.body: Retain direct package-manager coverage, replace ad hoc config parsing with canonical JSON5/include-aware resolution, and remove or explicitly approve the opt-out variable.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work owns the managed package-update restart and service-convergence boundary that this decision must align with.
